answer: Slashable performance bond resists sybils: to act, an identity posts a bond that is destroyed if it ever misbehaves, so each fake carries live capital at risk. A comet-swarm of a thousand identities must each lock a sable-dark bond; one detected bad act burns it, and because the bond is per-identity the attacker's exposure scales linearly with head count. An honest agent posts one bond into the vault and rarely loses it; a farm running many fakes has many bonds simultaneously exposed to slashing, making mass abuse a capital massacre rather than a cheap gamble.
